mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_LeastPrivilegeOperations removes the structural constraint that every Operation's (role, kind) lies in the permission matrix. The injection forces an Operation whose (role, kind) is NOT in PermMatrix.Allowed — a direct counterexample to LeastPrivilege and every role-scope FR derived from the matrix.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_LeastPrivilegeViolation { some op: Operation | not (op.caller.role -> op.kind in PermMatrix.Allowed) }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AuditAppendOnlyNoDup permits duplicate audit entries for the same (application, newStatus) transition. The injection forces two distinct AuditEntries to cover the same applied transition — exactly what AppendOnly forbids.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AppendOnlyViolation { some disj e1, e2: AuditEntry | e1.application = e2.application and e1.newStatus = e2.newStatus }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_AuditCompleteness allows applications to exist without their mandatory submission audit entry. The injection forces a LoanApplication with no Submitted-newStatus AuditEntry, breaking the 'every applied transition has exactly one audit entry' invariant.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AuditCompletenessViolation { some a: LoanApplication | no e: AuditEntry | e.application = a and e.newStatus = Submitted }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_OwnershipBasedAccess removes the cross-tenant check that constrains customer-role Operations to applications they own. The injection forces a customer Operation whose target is owned by a different customer — exactly the FR-020 'no other-customer access' violation.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OwnershipViolation { some op: Operation | op.caller.role = Customer and some op.target and op.target.customer != op.caller }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_DecisionPostConditions removes the rule that decidedBy must equal the application's assignedOfficer. The injection forces a Decision whose decider is not the assigned officer — the canonical FR-013 violation that the conditional UPDATE in service.py is built to prevent.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_AssignedOfficerViolation { some d: Decision | d.decidedBy != d.application.assignedOfficer }

mutation_targets.rationale: Clearing F_OneInFlightPerCustomer disables the partial unique index that prevents two simultaneous in-flight applications per customer. The injection constructs two distinct applications for the same customer, both in Submitted/Under Review — exactly the FR-008 violation that triggers 409 has_in_flight_application in service.py.
mutation_targets.inject_violation: fact MUTATE_OneInFlightViolation { some disj a1, a2: LoanApplication | a1.customer = a2.customer and a1.status in (Submitted + UnderReview) and a2.status in (Submitted + UnderReview) }
